newsitem.title: GERMANY: BHF Bank says CEO to step down in May.
newsitem.headline: BHF Bank says CEO to step down in May.

text.p: Germany's BHF Bank AG said on Wednesday its management board chairman Wolfgang Strutz would step down on May 13 at his own request, for health reasons.

In a statement, BHF said Strutz would be replaced by Ernst Michael Kruse, formerly vice-chairman of the board at Chase Manhattan Corporation, New York, who is to join the BHF management board on February 1.
BHF said its supervisory board had on Wednesday decided to honour a request from Strutz, 63, to leave his position.

Strutz, who has been part of BHF's senior management since 1983, would remain closely connected with BHF, the bank said, and would retain several positions on supervisory board of companies linked with BHF.
"On the basis of his thorough experiences in banking, he (Strutz) helped to develop crucial strategies for BHF Bank," the bank said.
BHF said the appointment of Ernst Michel Kruse underscored BHF's long established international strategic direction.

Kruse, 53, was responsible for Chase Bank's wholesale banking business until the bank's merger with Chemical Banking Corp. As vice-chairman of Chase Manhatten, Kruse was responsible for finances, risk management and global services.
BHF also said it had appointed Alfred Moeckel, hitherto a deputy member of its management board, to be a full board member effective February 1.
